title.narrative: ROAS : Japan village project (2nd phase of social housing complex) – Emergency support to returnees in northern part of Iraq towards durable solutions, including adaptation to Climate Change

description.narrative:
The project aims to strengthen social stabilization targeting returnees taking into account durable solutions, including the adaptation to climate change through (a) construction of social housing complex, and (b) relevant vocational trainings and public outreach campaign. The project will be implemented in the targeted area of Mosul (Rajm Hadeed, Aluboor), Ninewa Governorate, which the municipality of Mosul has positioned as the residential area for returnees under the Mosul Master Plan, upon the liberation from the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL).
The project aims to construct social housing units and public infrastructure in coordination with the local authorities with the approach of greener solutions and sustainability by utilizing environmentally friendly products in coordination with the UN-Habitat HQ, regional, and country offices, and other humanitarian actors, including UN sister agencies.
The project takes a community-based approach to address multiple challenges faced in Mosul, Ninewa governorate. The target areas and facilities will be selected based on the rapid field assessment conducted by UN-Habitat, taking into consideration the needs, physical level of damage, and socio-economic vulnerability of the expected beneficiaries. Through these activities, the project will target different groups of vulnerable returnees who left IDP camps. Local implementing partners, companies, and labourers will be engaged and employed for all construction activities under the project to help revitalization of the local economy and to enhance the sense of ownership and sustainability.
The project also takes synergies and an integrated approach by linking UN-Habitat’s activities to other projects in the Mosul area supported by other donors or implemented by other organizations, in particular, by collaborating closely with the Mosul Durable Solutions Area Based Coordination (ABC) Group/Joint Coordination Forum (JDF) formed by UN agencies, NGOs, and donors operating in Mosul for peacebuilding.
Additionally, the project takes greener solutions and incorporates a sustainability approach by utilising environmentally friendly approaches, and raising awareness on climate change by utilising national, regional, and global knowledge and experience of UN-Habitat.
The project will incorporate capacity development and awareness-raising in response to the negative impact on the climate change, including degradation of the agricultural sector and current drought in Iraq, which exacerbates the surging prices of daily living expenses of basic foods, towards the most vulnerable returnees.
UN-Habitat engineers and community mobilization officers will constantly be engaged on site throughout the project, conducting the field assessments, communicating with community members and local authorities on a daily basis, and supervising the field activities closely, which ensures the high quality of the work conducted.
Under the project, community members will be equipped with the necessary construction and rehabilitation skills through tailored vocational training sessions. In past projects implemented by UN-Habitat in conflict-affected areas of Iraq using the same approach, participation in the vocational training enabled returnees to gain skills that are necessary and relevant to be employed by private companies working on construction works. UN-Habitat conditioned its contractors to employ the trainees and monitored the employment record of the trainees. This initiative has not only helped with job creation, but also allowed returnees to gain cash funds. Under the circumstance where small business loans are not easily accessible, such cash income helped returnees to start their own businesses. This approach will thus empowers community members both socially and economically, increases community ownership, and encourages targeted communities to solve their problems independently, which is the key to sustainable returns.
Main Expected Accomplishment:
Outcome 1: Living conditions in the targeted communities/neighborhoods are improved through construction of social housing units with environmentally friendly approaches. Disability-inclusive development is to be taken into account as an essential condition for a sustainable future which is in line with the UN disability inclusion strategy to accelerate peace and security, human rights, and development.
Output 1-1: Social housing units are constructed in the site to accommodate 72 households (maximum).
Outcome 2: Livelihoods and self-reliance of returnees in the targeted communities/neighborhoods, including unemployed young men and women are enhanced through improving their access to marketplaces and capacity development and awareness-raising.
